extracted.intended_audience: math educators, learners, and content creators (e.g., teachers, explainer-video makers, self-learners)
extracted.subtask_description: A collection of principles and practical heuristics for explaining, learning, and creating math content focused on intuition, visuals, storytelling, and active problem-solving, distilled from Grant Sanderson's practices (3Blue1Brown). Useful for educators, video creators, and self-directed learners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Motivate math as an art form
rubrics_metrics.description: Motivate math as an art form by exploring puzzles and problems with intrinsic beauty — those that are initially challenging but become doable and beautiful after a shift in perspective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Seek examples that evoke wonder, aesthetic pleasure, and conceptual elegance rather than only emphasizing utility. Anti-pattern: presenting topics only as tools or formulae without showing their aesthetic or conceptual appeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use storytelling in explanations
rubrics_metrics.description: Treat math lessons as stories: appeal to emotion, include elements like comedy or characters, create a mystery that needs resolution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Structure explanations with narrative arcs (motivation, problem, tension, resolution). This helps maintain attention and frames technical material meaningfully. Anti-pattern: dry, decontextualized presentation with no narrative or emotional hooks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Put visuals first
rubrics_metrics.description: When possible, present visuals first and then articulate their meaning so learners can develop a sense of ownership over concepts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use animations or diagrams to give an intuitive feel before introducing formalism. This encourages internalization. Anti-pattern: starting with abstract definitions and symbols before any visual or intuitive grounding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resist starting with abstractions
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid the common tendency to begin explanations with the general abstract thing once you understand a topic; start with concrete/intuitive instances instead.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lead learners from concrete examples toward abstraction. Anti-pattern: textbook-style abstract-first exposition that can alienate beginners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Education as 'educe' (bring understanding out)
rubrics_metrics.description: View teaching as bringing understanding out from within the student, not merely pushing information in.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design activities that elicit learners' existing intuitions and build on them, e.g., guided discovery and projects. Anti-pattern: one-way lecturing without opportunities for learners to construct their own understanding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prioritize motivation over mere explanation quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Motivation is a primary limiting factor for new learners; it's often more important than perfectly polished explanations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on what motivates learners to engage (curiosity, projects, community) rather than only optimizing clarity in isolation. Anti-pattern: concentrating solely on didactic clarity while neglecting why learners should care.

rubrics_metrics.name: Facilitate projects and curate resources (educator role)
rubrics_metrics.description: The educator's role includes facilitating projects, identifying student interests, and curating appropriate resources beyond simply giving explanations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide project prompts, recommended next steps, and resource paths. Encourage application and guided exploration. Anti-pattern: only delivering lectures without scaffolding application or discovery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encourage active learning and doing problems
rubrics_metrics.description: Active interaction (problems, exercises, teaching) leads to far greater retention than passive reading or listening.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Build frequent problem practice and opportunities to teach into learning paths. Quantified heuristic quoted: ~10% retained from reading, ~20% from listening, ~70% from active interaction, ~90% from teaching. Anti-pattern: passively consuming videos/lectures without practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Embrace struggling as part of learning
rubrics_metrics.description: Struggling with problems is integral; don't move on until you've worked through exercises and experienced productive difficulty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design learning schedules that require actual problem-solving, and normalize temporary confusion as healthy. Anti-pattern: skipping practice or treating solution-reading as equivalent to problem-solving.

rubrics_metrics.name: Value reinvention and rediscovery
rubrics_metrics.description: The deepest learning comes from rediscovery — reconstructing ideas yourself gives strong ownership of concepts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include tasks where learners attempt to rediscover results or derive from basic principles. Anti-pattern: always presenting polished finished proofs without opportunities to reconstruct steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledge gaps and intellectual humility
rubrics_metrics.description: Learners and teachers should acknowledge gaps in understanding; recognizing limits fosters growth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Model admitting uncertainty and show how to investigate gaps. Anti-pattern: presenting oneself as infallible or masking confusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preview problems before reading
rubrics_metrics.description: Look at chapter-end problems before reading the chapter — the ones that make a little sense are ideal to think about and prime learning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use problem previews to generate curiosity and identify which parts of the text will be most salient. Anti-pattern: reading straight through text without engaging with problems early.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be flexible in learning strategies
rubrics_metrics.description: Success often depends less on innate intuition and more on being willing to try different ways of learning and switching strategies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage learners to switch books, formats, or approaches if progress stalls. Anti-pattern: rigid adherence to one method despite lack of progress.

rubrics_metrics.name: Give things meaningful names
rubrics_metrics.description: Naming concepts meaningfully aids problem-solving and understanding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When introducing objects or maneuvers, choose names that capture structure or function to help reasoning. Anti-pattern: opaque or purely formal labels that obscure intuition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Leverage symmetry as a technique
rubrics_metrics.description: Use symmetry to simplify and guide problem-solving; respecting mathematical symmetries often yields rewards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Actively look for invariances and symmetrical structure in problems to reduce complexity. Anti-pattern: ignoring symmetry and pursuing brute-force manipulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ask simpler versions of the problem
rubrics_metrics.description: When stuck, pose a simpler variant to gain insight that can scale back up to the original problem.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Solve toy cases, reduce parameters, or examine boundary/special cases to form hypotheses. Anti-pattern: confronting full complexity immediately without reduction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Draw pictures and instantiate numbers
rubrics_metrics.description: Visualizing problems (draw a picture, use coordinates or concrete numbers) is a powerful first step.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage sketches, diagrams, and concrete instantiations before abstract manipulation. Anti-pattern: proceeding algebraically without geometric intuition or examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reflect on solutions to identify missing instincts
rubrics_metrics.description: After reading a solution, don't just check understanding — reflect on what instinct you lacked and how you could have been led to that solution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Teach learners to extract heuristics from solutions and rehearse those instincts. Anti-pattern: passively reading solutions and moving on.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use teaching as a learning tool
rubrics_metrics.description: Actively teaching material is one of the strongest methods for consolidating knowledge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Have learners explain topics to peers or create content (videos, write-ups) as part of learning. Anti-pattern: never attempting to teach or articulate one's understanding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be willing to change resources (toss a book aside)
rubrics_metrics.description: Find learning materials that meet you at the right level and style; abandon resources that are too easy, too hard, or misaligned with goals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage switching texts or formats to maintain progress and motivation. Anti-pattern: persisting with an unsuitable textbook out of inertia.

rubrics_metrics.name: Don't just give the answer—provide the surrounding story
rubrics_metrics.description: Adding the narrative/context around a solution (why it matters, how one might discover it) adds value beyond the bare technique.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When presenting solutions, include motivation, failed approaches, and the idea-space that led to the solution. Anti-pattern: presenting only polished final answers with no context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Favor authenticity over watered-down simplification
rubrics_metrics.description: Learners prefer authentic material that treats them like future experts rather than overly diluted 'watered down' versions that talk down to them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide challenging authentic glimpses into real material while scaffolding appropriately. Anti-pattern: oversimplification that removes essential structure to make material superficially easier.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guard against the 'pedagogical curse'
rubrics_metrics.description: Mathematicians can undervalue pedagogical clarity relative to rigor, making material harder than necessary; prioritize making things clear pedagogically.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deliberately allocate effort to pedagogical design (order of presentation, examples, visuals) as much as to technical correctness. Anti-pattern: assuming that technical mastery ensures good teaching without adaptation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treat online videos as partial—require active follow-up
rubrics_metrics.description: Videos are good for intuition but are only part of learning; they must be complemented by active problem-solving and other practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pair videos with problem sets, projects, or prompts to apply ideas. Anti-pattern: binge-watching explanatory videos while neglecting exercises.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use programmatic animation selectively and design workflows
rubrics_metrics.description: When using programmatic tools (like Manim), separate what should be programmatic from what doesn't need to be; choose workflows that don't constrain creativity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design animations to clarify key ideas; avoid overengineering visuals that obscure intent. Anti-pattern: forcing every idea into programmatic animation even when simpler media suffice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Share tools and methods (open source and transparency)
rubrics_metrics.description: Open-sourcing code and revealing methods (e.g., Manim) helps others learn how materials are made and enables community growth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make production assets available and document workflows to amplify impact. Anti-pattern: hoarding tools or leaving consumers mystified about how content was produced.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow personal curiosity and start low-stakes
rubrics_metrics.description: Begin with topics that genuinely spark your interest and with low-stakes projects to build momentum and authenticity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use personal projects to explore and learn; keep initial efforts low-pressure to encourage experimentation. Anti-pattern: choosing projects solely for perceived prestige or immediate payoff.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cultivate community and peer motivation
rubrics_metrics.description: Peers and community are primary motivators; learning often accelerates through social engagement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage study groups, discussion forums, and peer feedback. Anti-pattern: solitary, isolated study with no peer interaction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aim for deep intuitive ownership (e.g., 'you could have invented calculus')
rubrics_metrics.description: Set the goal that learners should feel they could have invented the topic — i.e., achieve deep, generative understanding rather than rote knowledge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design sequences that scaffold from concrete problems to the conceptual leap, enabling learners to reconstruct the theory. Anti-pattern: goal-setting that only targets procedural fluency without conceptual generativity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use AI and tooling as strong helpers, not replacements
rubrics_metrics.description: AI is a powerful tool (often better than many people at routine tasks) but not yet a wholesale substitute for top human mathematicians; treat it as an augmenting resource.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leverage AI for simulations, drafts, or assistance while preserving human-guided insight and oversight. Anti-pattern: over-relying on AI to replace the reflective/problem-solving process of learners.
